title: Clique trees, subtree representations and chordal treewidth
abstract: Develops rooted clique forests with the running-intersection property, constructs them from perfect elimination orders of finite chordal graphs, characterizes chordality by their existence, and obtains maximal-clique, separator, and counting results. Also characterizes chordality under retained-clique gluing of induced pieces, with exact vertex and edge inclusion-exclusion identities. The original library was extracted as a reusable byproduct of the published Paper IV formalization of the chordal-graph case of Erdős problem #81; this library is not by itself a proof of that paper's partition bound. Gavril's characterization supplies exact finite-tree subtree representations and the converse to chordality. Finite subtree Helly places every finite clique in a bag of any tree decomposition and gives optimal chordal treewidth. The supplied representation includes an empty connector; no minimal-host or runtime bound is claimed.

informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.exists_isPEO: Every finite chordal graph admits a perfect elimination order.
informal.SimpleGraph.isChordal_iff_nonempty_cliqu: A finite graph is chordal if and only if it has a rooted clique tree.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.exists_maximalCliq: A nonempty finite chordal graph has a clique tree whose distinct bags are precisely its maximal cliques, with no more bags than vertices.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueTree.exists_parent_eq_: In a clique tree, each minimal separator of two reachable vertices is the intersection of two adjacent bags.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueTree.card_eq_sum_card_: The total bag size minus the total parent-child bag intersection size equals the number of graph vertices.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueTree.toSubtreeRepresen: A finite rooted clique forest gives nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite host tree, with adjacency of distinct source vertices exactly equivalent to intersection of their assigned sets. Empty and disconnected source graphs are supported through one empty connector node.
informal.SimpleGraph.isChordal_iff_nonempty_subtr: A finite graph on a vertex type in Type is chordal if and only if it has an exact representation by nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite tree.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsTree.finite_subtree_helly: A finite pairwise-intersecting family of nonempty connected vertex sets of a finite tree has a common vertex; the empty family is also allowed.
informal.Utilities.Treewidth.TreeDecomposition.ex: Every finite clique is contained in one bag of any tree decomposition.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.treewidth_succ_eq_: For every finite nonempty chordal graph on a vertex type in Type, its natural treewidth plus one equals its clique number.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.exists_optimal_tre: A finite nonempty chordal graph admits a tree decomposition whose width plus one is its clique number.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueGluing.isChordal_iff: If two induced pieces cover a finite graph, their overlap is a clique, and no edge joins their exclusive parts, the graph is chordal exactly when both pieces are chordal. Overlap edges are retained.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueGluing.card_vertices_a: The vertex count of the graph plus the overlap size equals the sum of the vertex counts of the two covering pieces.
informal.SimpleGraph.CliqueGluing.card_edges_add_: The graph edge count plus the number of pairs in the retained clique overlap equals the sum of the induced pieces' edge counts.
